data.name: Mamatha
data.gender_notes: Mamatha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Mamatha refers to the mother of the universe and the goddess of nourishment and protection. She is also known as Parvati, the consort of Lord Shiva. The name Mamatha carries the meaning “Mother of the Universe” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mamatha usually hope their child will grow to embody mother of the universe and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes maternal love, nourishment, and protection.
data.etymology: Mamatha belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Mother of the Universe.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mamatha total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

It is a tribute to Parvati, the eternal lover of Lord Shiva and the embodiment of feminine love, compassion, and nourishment. Mamatha is also revered as a symbol of a good and loving mother figure.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mamatha holds deep spiritual significance, being derived from the divine goddess Parvati. It represents a connection to the divine feminine and the powers of creation, nourishment, and protection. A person named Mamatha is believed to embody these qualities and to have a spiritual bond with the divine goddess of love, compassion, and nourishment.
